about: Telekommunikation (389.138) at TU Wien after the lecture slides of Goiser (2016), thirteen sets, with the course formulary of March 2017 (Notation, Definitionen und Formelsammlung). Slide numbers are the printed ones, read in the slides' text layer on 1 Nov 2026; where the text layer garbled a formula, the reading was checked against a second route in tests/unit/core.test.js, and the note says so. No exercise collection or exam with worked solutions was at hand, so the practice questions are the slides' own worked examples (their slide named) or were worked by hand from the slides' equations, as each says. tests/unit/labs-data.test.js recomputes every answer with the core and fails if they disagree. Sampling, the Fourier transform and filters are the Signals and Systems lab's; free-space link budgets, fading and delay spread are the Electrodynamics lab's.

practice.question: A full-scale sine is quantised by linear PCM with 8 bits. What signal-to-quantisation-noise ratio does the 6 dB rule give?
practice.solution: SNQR_dB = 4.8 + 6 · 8 − 3 = 49.8 dB, with α = 2 (3 dB) for a sine. Exactly: 10 log(3 · 2¹⁶ / 2) = 49.9 dB.
practice.source: Worked by hand from Goiser (2016), set 2, slides 46–47

practice.question: PCM30 carries 32 channels, each sampled at 8 kHz with 8 bits. What is its bit rate?
practice.solution: 8 kHz · 8 bit = 64 kbit/s a channel; 32 · 64 kbit/s = 2.048 Mbit/s.
practice.source: Worked example, Goiser (2016), set 2, slide 63

practice.question: An 8-bit PCM link has a bit error probability of 10⁻⁵. What SNR is left after decoding?

practice.question: Polar NRZ reaches a bit error probability of 10⁻⁵ at E/N0 = 9.6 dB with a matched filter. What does unipolar NRZ reach at 9.6 dB of mean energy?
practice.solution: Unipolar: ½ erfc(√(E/2N0)), with E/N0 = 10^0.96 = 9.12: ½ erfc(√4.56) = ½ erfc(2.135) = 1.26·10⁻³, over a hundred times worse. It needs 3 dB more, 12.6 dB, for 10⁻⁵.
practice.source: Worked by hand from the course formulary of March 2017, Table 2, and Goiser (2016), set 3, slide 55

practice.question: The same BPSK link, at 9.6 dB with the carrier right, samples a quarter of a bit late (ε = 0.25). What is the bit error probability?
practice.solution: Pe = ½ Q(4.27) + ½ Q(4.27 · (1 − 2 · 0.25)) = ½ · 10⁻⁵ + ½ Q(2.14) = 0.5·10⁻⁵ + ½ · 1.6·10⁻² = 8.2·10⁻³: the bits after a change of sign lose half their integral.

labs.title: A telephone channel, from the voice to the receiver's noise
labs.idea: One voice channel through the whole course: sampled and quantised, coded, put on QPSK symbols and raised-cosine pulses, received through the slides' superheterodyne receiver. Every step sets the rate of the next; the receiver's noise sets the bit errors, and they the voice's SNR.

practice.question: A voice channel is sampled at 8 kHz with 8 bit and protected by a Hamming (7,4) code. What is the bit rate on the channel?
practice.solution: Rb = 8 kHz · 8 bit = 64 kbit/s; the code sends 7 bits for every 4: Rc = 64 · 7/4 = 112 kbit/s.
